accepted.hypothesis: Killing the single front-end pod will cause the front-end service to have no healthy endpoints, resulting in HTTP 503 for all golden journey steps.
accepted.expected_invariant: front-end service must return HTTP 200 for all steps
accepted.validation_plan: Inject pod_kill on workload/front-end, then call front-end service endpoints /, /catalogue, /login, /orders and verify HTTP status codes.
accepted.recovery_expectation: Pod restarts and service recovers after Kubernetes reschedules.
accepted.weakness_surface: single replica workload with no redundancy

accepted.hypothesis: Introducing 500ms network delay on the front-end service will cause timeouts for the golden journey steps, leading to HTTP 500 or 504.
accepted.expected_invariant: front-end service must return HTTP 200 for all steps
accepted.validation_plan: Inject network_delay on service/front-end, then call front-end service endpoints and verify HTTP status codes.
accepted.recovery_expectation: After delay duration, service returns to normal.
accepted.weakness_surface: synchronous downstream call without evidenced timeout

accepted.recovery_expectation: After loss duration, service returns to normal.
accepted.weakness_surface: synchronous downstream call without evidenced timeout
